failures.nodes: source=game score; target=whole previous sequence of actions and observations; cause=game score; effect=whole previous sequence
failures.evidence: Note that in general the game score may depend on the whole previous sequence of actions and observations
failures.reason: cause/effect polarity REVERSED: sentence says score depends on sequence, so cause should be sequence -> effect score; edge asserts the score causes its own past

failures.nodes: source=feedback about an action; target=many thousands of time-steps
failures.evidence: feedback about an action may only be received after many thousands of time-steps have elapsed
failures.reason: temporal delay statement misread as causal influence; feedback does not influence the elapsed time-steps

failures.nodes: source=current situation; target=current screen xt; cause=current situation; effect=current screen xt
failures.evidence: it is impossible to fully understand the current situation from only the current screen xt
failures.reason: epistemic limitation (partial observability) misread as dependence; situation does not influence the screen

failures.nodes: subject=sequences of actions and observations st; definition=algorithm; object=sequences st
failures.evidence: sequences of actions and observations, st = x1, a1, x2, ..., at-1, xt, are input to the algorithm
failures.reason: 'are input to the algorithm' is an input relation, not a definition; st is not defined-as 'algorithm'

failures.evidence: Execute action at in emulator and observe reward rt and image x_{t+1}
failures.reason: algorithm step (execute action in environment) is not a measurement relation; the emulator does not measure the action

failures.evidence: Store transition (phi_t, a_t, r_t, phi_{t+1}) in D
failures.reason: storage-in-replay-memory misread as composition with direction inverted; D is composed of transitions, not a component of one transition

failures.evidence: estimate the action-value function by using the Bellman equation as an iterative update, Q_{i+1}(s,a) = E[...]
failures.reason: Bellman equation is the update law itself, not an input quantity; binding it to the input slot is a law-vs-input category confusion

failures.nodes: from=value iteration algorithms; to=optimal action-value function
failures.evidence: Such value iteration algorithms converge to the optimal action-value function
failures.reason: 'converge to' is a convergence guarantee, not a generalization/extension relation

failures.evidence: it is common to use a function approximator to estimate the action-value function
failures.reason: sentence states usage-for-estimation, no improvement claim at all
